A Reputed Financial Institution invites applications from dynamic, experienced, and result-oriented professionals for the position of Chief Operating Officer (COO). The selected candidate will play a key leadership role in driving operational excellence and supporting the effective execution of the institution’s strategic priorities.

Required Role : Chief Operating Officer (COO)
Position : Senior Manager / Chief Manager / Assistant General Manager
Required No. : 1
Required Location : Head Office, Kathmandu
Age : Minimum 25 years and not exceeding 50 years
Qualification : Master’s Degree from recognized university in the field of Management/Economics or equivalent qualification in related discipline.
Experience : Minimum 15 years of experience in recognized Banks or Financial Institutions in Nepal.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Oversee banking operations to enhance efficiency, productivity, service quality, and cost effectiveness.
  •  Drive process improvement, digital transformation, automation, and operational excellence.
  • Ensure strong internal controls, risk management, governance, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience.
  • Strengthen customer service, financial inclusion, and accessibility of banking services.
  • Monitor organizational performance against key priorities and implement corrective measures as necessary.
  • Lead, develop, and mentor high-performing teams and strengthen the institution’s leadership pipeline.
  • Provide strategic and operational leadership to ensure effective execution of the institution’s strategic plans.
  •  Advise Senior Executives on operational performance, risks, opportunities, and strategic priorities.

Interested and eligible candidates are requested to send their updated CV along with cover letter and supporting documents no later than 15th September 2026 at: vacancy.institution@gmail.com

Note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The National Federation of Women Living with HIV and AIDS (NFWLHA), formerly known as the Women’s Network against HIV & AIDS (WONAHA), was initially established as a loose network in 2006 and was officially registered in 2007 with a vision to create a just and equitable society for women and children infected and affected with HIV, so that they can live a productive, empowered and dignified life, free from stigma and discrimination. Underpinned by guiding principles of gender equity and human rights, evidence-based planning, programming, and policy advocacy, NFWLHA has broadened its strategic intervention areas over the last nine years, focusing mainly on strengthening and capacity development of the network, knowledge management for evidence-based policy advocacy and community system strengthening. Currently, there are 35 community-based organizations (CBOs) affiliated with NFWLHA representing Nepal’s seven provinces, all led by women living with HIV (WLHIV).

Position: Sr. Finance Assistant-1
No. of Vacancy: 1
Duty Station: NFWLHA Central Office, Kathmandu (Frequent travel to program district)
Reports/responsible to: Finance Head
Supervisory Responsibilities: Program cum finance officers

1. Purpose of the Position:

The Finance Assistant will provide support to the finance department in managing the financial operations of NFWLHA. This will include assisting with accounting tasks, processing payments, maintaining financial records, and ensuring compliance with financial policies and procedures.

2. Major Responsibilities:

Accounting Support

  • Assist in day-to-day accounting operations, including data entry, record keeping, and financial transactions.
  • Prepare and process payments to vendors, partners, and staff.
  • Reconcile bank statements and other financial reports.
  • Maintain accurate and organized financial files and records.

Financial Management

  • Assist in the preparation of budgets and financial reports.
  • Track expenses and monitor budget performance.
  • Support the financial management of projects and programs.
  • Ensure compliance with financial policies, procedures, and donor requirements.

Administrative Support

  • Provide general administrative and clerical support to the finance department.
  • Assist with the preparation of audit documents and financial statements.
  • Manage petty cash and other financial transactions.

Reporting and recording

  • Maintain all financial records and books of account as per the NFWLHA policy.
  • Prepare a monthly statement of expenditure.
  • Assist the Administration and Finance Manager and Officer in preparing financial statements for the Program Manager, Coordinator, and the Executive Committee.
  • Produce financial information, and budget-monitoring information regularly to help the Administration and Finance Officer, Program Manager, and Coordinator to monitor budgets.

Meeting and communications

  • Participate in meetings to ensure that information is shared with appropriate staff members.
  • Fulfill and participate in finance-related meetings with concerned stakeholders and funding agencies in the absence of administration and finance officers.

Organizational Development

  • Follow NFWLHA’s formulated policies, internal rules and regulations and contribute to the achievement of long-term objectives of the organization.
  • Actively participate in the process of organizational change process and implement Strategic plan directions.

3. Education and Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in finance or accounting, preferably in a non-profit organization.
  • Strong knowledge of basic accounting principles and procedures.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other accounting software.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Fluency in Nepali and English (written and spoken).
  • Knowledge of HIV/AIDS-related issues, gender equity, and social inclusion (preferred).
  • Preference will be given to candidates with experience in Global Fund projects and working knowledge of FAMOUS, TrueBooks, and Tally accounting software.

Position: Provincial Supervisor
No. of Vacancy: 1
Duty Station: Madhesh Province- Janakpur
Reports/responsible to: Program Associate
Supervisory Responsibilities: Program Coordinator

1. Purpose of the Position:

The provincial supervisor is responsible for supervising the day-to-day operation of the care and support program in their assigned province.

2. Major Responsibilities:

Programme Planning

  • Supervise and manage the operation of care and support programs within the province to align with the budget and work plan of the program.
  • Ensure the implementation of HIV care and support programs at the province level aligns with national standards and guidelines for care and support programs.
  • Set clear goals and objectives for HIV care and support programs such as improving access to ART, counseling services, and community-based care.
  • Programme Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation
  • Ensure the services are delivered efficiently at the community level and at healthcare facilities in the districts of the province.
  • Assess program impact and make adjustments as needed to improve effectiveness.
  • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of HIV program service delivery in the districts of the province, ensuring targets are met and program goals are achieved.

Coordination and collaboration

  • Coordination with the provincial and local government, health facilities, district member organizations, and community-based organizations to enhance service delivery.
  • Closely coordinate and communicate with the CBOs and district-level field team within the province.
  • Promote team collaboration and ensure the sharing of knowledge and best practices.

Reporting

  • Receive reports from the districts, monitor the accuracy and quality of data, support in data cleaning, consolidate the reports and analyze the data to prepare provincial reports.
  • Maintain accurate records of program including beneficiary tracking, service provision, and outcomes.
  • Ensure regular and accurate reporting on the progress of HIV care and support programs.

Staff Management and Development

  • Supervise and manage the work of the district care and support teams, delegate tasks, and set priorities and deadlines.
  • Provide guidance, support, and mentorship to the staff of the districts in the province to ensure optimal performance.
  • Organize and get involved in regular training sessions and professional development opportunities to build capacity and improve service delivery.

Meeting/Communication

  • Participate in and organize regular meetings with team members to discuss challenges, progress, and priorities.
  • Ensure effective communication within the team and with external partners, providing timely updates and clarifying information.
  • Promote transparent communication within the NFWLHA team regarding program successes, challenges, and financial matters.

Organizational Development

  • Collaborate with the related stakeholders and the NFWLHA team on advocacy initiatives aimed at advancing the organizational goal and objective.
  • Implement formulated policies, rules and regulations, and long-term objectives of the organization at national, regional, and district levels and provide appropriate feedback.
  • Actively participate in the process of organizational change process and implement work plan directions.

3. Education and Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Science, Public Health, or a related area is preferred
  • At least 2 to 3 years of experience in the HIV program in the supervisory role
  • Strong leadership and people management skills
  • Knowledge of MS Office, Excel, and PowerPoint and data management skills
  • Strong interpersonal skills and written and verbal communication
  • Excellent coordination skills, ability to handle multiple tasks and work under pressure.

To Apply:

Interested and eligible candidates are requested to apply with CV, Reference contact details, Cover letter with expected salary and relevant certificates at nfwlha.vacancy@gmail.com before 11th September, 2026, Friday. Interviews will begin on rolling basis and the best fit candidate will be selected immediately.

NFWLHA recognizes that it has the responsibility to respect and promote gender equality and the safety and protection of all. NFWLHA has a ZERO-tolerance policy regarding abuse. NFWLHA reserves the right of conducting a background check of the potential candidates. Only Shortlisted candidate will be contacted.

​About CBM Global

​CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

  • Break the cycle of poverty and disability
  • Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
  • Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.

We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

​About the Role

​CBM Global Nepal has initiated a humanitarian response in areas affected by the devastating flash floods in the Bhotekoshi River and downstream river systems. The response covers affected communities in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts and focuses on mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), basic needs assistance, provision of assistive devices, rehabilitation services, and advocacy and technical support to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the overall humanitarian response.

The Finance and Administration Officer is responsible for overseeing the overall financial and administrative functions of the humanitarian response project, working in close coordination with the Country Office Finance and Administration teams.

​S/he ensures effective financial management of the project by monitoring the utilization of project budgets in line with approved work plans, and CBM Global’s policies and procedures. S/he works closely with partner organizations to provide guidance and support on grant management, financial reporting, and compliance. Additionally, s/he provides administrative and procurement support as needed to ensure the efficient functioning of the country office and successful implementation of the project.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Oversee the financial management of the project in close coordination with the project team and partner organizations
  • Establish, implement, and maintain financial procedures and internal controls in line with organisational policies and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Review financial documents, receipts, invoices, and supporting documentation to ensure transactions are accurate, complete, valid, verifiable, and authorized.
  • Monitor financial risks and recommend corrective actions to ensure sound financial management.​

Budget Management

  • Monitor partner budget implementation rates in relation to fund transfers and ensure timely disbursement of project funds to partners.
  • Support periodic budget reviews, revisions, and amendments as required.
  • Prepare monthly forecasts, budget plans, and expenditure reports in collaboration with project teams.
  • Analyze budget variances and provide recommendations to support effective financial decision-making.​

Partner Support

  • Ensure partner staffs are aware and comply with the statutory regulations, CBM policies and guidelines, and partnership agreements.
  • Provide required support to the partners for effective management of project finances, preparation of financial reports and others as required.
  • Validate partners’ financial transactions to ensure accuracy, completeness and timeliness.
  • ​Guide and monitor procurement processes in the partner organizations.
  • Conduct monitoring of field activities in collaboration with the project team and partner organization, as necessary

​Admin and Procurement Support

  • ​Provide administrative, logistical, and operational support for country office and project activities.
  • Support procurement processes in the country office.
  • Process vendor invoices and ensure timely payment in accordance with organizational procedures​

Safeguarding

  • ​Accountable for ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with CBM Global’s programmes are safeguarded to the greatest extent possible.
  • Responsible for ensuring compliance to all aspects of the CBM Global Safeguarding policy and associated standards and procedures.​

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for a candidate who brings the following experience and qualities:

All the following requirements are Essential, unless marked with a * when they are Desirable.

​

Experience and knowledge

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in finance and operations, preferably in International NGOs.
  • Demonstrated experience in project financial management, including budgeting, financial controls, financial monitoring, reporting. etc.
  • Experience in partner management and support.
  • Experience working with humanitarian response and/or recovery projects
  • Sound knowledge of financial management principles, accounting standards, and applicable laws and regulations.​

Skills/competencies/personal qualities

  • Strong planning and organizational abilities with a results-oriented approach.
  • Excellent analytical skills with the ability to interpret and present financial information effectively.
  • Competent in using office packages and accounting software.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing work demands in emergency contexts.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and respond to dynamic environments.
  • Alignment to CBM Global values (Our Vision, Mission and Values | CBM Global) and Safeguarding Policy (CBM-Global-Policy-Safeguarding.pdf) and Code of Conduct (CBM-Global-Code-of-Conduct.pdf)

Qualifications, training, and education

  • ​Bachelor’s degree in management, accounting or relevant field of study.
  • Master’s degree preferred.

We welcome and encourage applications from people with lived experience of disability.

​

We proactively work on achieving a diverse and inclusive work environment for people from all backgrounds and abilities.

Why work with Us?

Flexible working: We believe flexible working is key to building the Organization of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. However, we think this role would work particularly well as a full-time role for 40 hours per week.

The Role

The Emergency Response Team provides timely, effective and accountable emergency assistance to populations affected by disasters and humanitarian crises. The team coordinates with government authorities, partners, communities and humanitarian actors to deliver quality humanitarian programming and strengthen local response capacity. To provide overall field-level leadership, coordination, representation, and oversight of Oxfam’s emergency response interventions in Nuwakot district, ensuring effective implementation by partner organizations and timely coordination with the Response Manager and humanitarian stakeholders. The role will support partners to deliver quality, accountable and gender-responsive humanitarian assistance to flood-affected communities while ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and humanitarian principles.

Who we’re looking for

We are looking for someone who has the following experience, knowledge and competencies.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Humanitarian Studies or a related field with a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience, OR a Master’s degree in a related field with a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience in humanitarian and emergency response programming.

Emergency Response Delivery

Lead and oversee timely, quality, and compliant implementation of emergency response activities, including assessments, planning, monitoring, risk management, and ensuring gender-responsive and accountable programming.

Coordination and Representation

Represent Oxfam in humanitarian coordination forums and maintain effective relationships with government authorities, partners, donors, UN agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated and effective response delivery.

Partnership Management

Manage and support implementing partners to ensure quality programme delivery, compliance with donor and Oxfam requirements, capacity strengthening, and accountability.

Team Management

Provide leadership and supervision to district response teams, foster collaboration and staff development, and ensure staff wellbeing, safeguarding compliance, and adherence to Oxfam values.

Monitoring, Learning and Reporting

Ensure effective monitoring, reporting, quality assurance, documentation of lessons learned, and regular communication on programme progress, risks, challenges, and opportunities.

What we offer

Oxfam is committed to providing a fair compensation package and to providing a flexible, supportive, working environment.

This role will provide you with an opportunity to make a difference in Oxfam by working closely with a group of passionate people that are specialists in their field of Gender, WASH and Water Governance, Humanitarian and DRM and so forth along with the national and international training and development opportunities. Our offer consists of fair pay and competitive benefits package. At Oxfam, we believe that every aspect of our work can lead to a positive outcome. If you have the same opinion, together with the ability to meet the challenges involved, this role offers scope for immense personal fulfilment – as well as outstanding opportunities to develop your career.

We offer:

We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits.

From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more.

You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer here.

Flexfam:

We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. We think this role would work particularly well as such as part-time, job share, hybrid.

How to apply:
As part of your online application, Please upload an up-to-date CV and a cover letter, clearly explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile by 10 September 2026.

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and Oxfam reserves the right to close the recruitment process and make an appointment before the closing date.

Our values and commitment to safeguarding

Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Oxfam GB engages. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Oxfam GB also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

About us

Oxfam is a global community who believe poverty isn’t inevitable. It’s an injustice that can be overcome. We are shop volunteers, women’s right activists, marathon runners, aid workers, coffee farmers, street fundraisers, goat herders, policy experts, campaigners, water engineers and more. And we won’t stop until everyone can live life without poverty for good.

Oxfam GB is a member of international confederation of 21 organisations working together with partners and local communities in the areas of humanitarian, development and campaigning, in more than 90 countries.

A thriving diverse Oxfam:

It’s people power that brings about change. To play our part as a global organisation working to overcome poverty and inequality, we need equality, diversity and inclusion across our community of staff, partners and volunteers. Together, we’re committed to becoming a more diverse workforce, better able to tackle the global challenges that face our world today.

To do that:

  • We need to dismantle the unequal power structures that exist everywhere, this including Oxfam and the wider development and charity sectors.
  • We need an inclusive Oxfam where everyone can bring who they are to our work and feels celebrated for the differences they bring.
  • We want and need everyone, and that means we need you.

Posiiton: Emergency Response Coordinator

Location: Nuwakot, Nepal

Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position

The Response Coordinator will offer technical assistance to the project, supporting the emergency response for the flooding in Rauswa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The coordinator will work under the direct supervision of the Country Director and will collaborate closely with the implementing and technical partners, as well as the Financial Service Provider. The coordinator will also establish strong relationships with humanitarian actors, agencies active in the targeted municipality and districts, and government officials to ensure the quality of project interventions, focusing mainly on the timely completion of activities within the given timeframe, avoiding sporadic distribution of support, and providing comprehensive support to selected households to meet multiple needs.

Essential Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Emergency Response Coordinator include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Lead the implementation of humanitarian response activities in accordance with the project plans, budgets, and timelines.
  • Ensure effective coordination and close engagement with stakeholders to lead project implementation, including endorsing vulnerability criteria and selecting beneficiaries.
  • Support execution of agreements with partner/s and Technical and Financial Service Providers (T/FSP) for project interventions.
  • Work with partners to undertake rapid market assessments to deploy sectoral CVA assistance, identify appropriate modalities for cash and voucher assistance, and produce reports.
  • Ensure project interventions adhere to quality standards, humanitarian principles, and organizational policies.
  • Extend technical support to partners through the MCN finance unit on financial and procurement procedures for CVA, disbursement mechanisms, and mobilization.
  • Support mobilization of T/FSPs for the deployment of digital CVA modalities.
  • Support orientation for vendors and enumerators, register flood-affected targeted households, and generate reports through TSP.
  • Facilitate the redemption of CVA assistance through electronic vouchers and cash transfers, working alongside T/FSPs.
  • Assist in undertaking Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) within two to four weeks of support through call centers.
  • Lead issue logs and ensure the project accountability matrix is duly established for accurate targeting and CVA programming.
  • Manage partner relations, facilitating regular coordination meetings to review progress, address challenges, and ensure timely implementation.
  • Participate in technical meetings with local authorities, clusters, NGOs, and relevant institutions.
  • Work closely with the Country CARM focal person to ensure participants, communities, and stakeholders are oriented on CARM and safeguarding, and that issues are managed per MC policy.
  • Prepare the project work plan and detailed implementation plan.
  • Track budget expenditure and prepare weekly, monthly, and final reports.
  • Lead the learning process of documentation and capture case stories from the field.

Safeguarding Responsbilities

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility

  • Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer

Accountability

  • Reports Directly To: Country Director
  • Works Directly With: Program Quality and Partnership Manager, Country CARM Focal point, and project technical partner team members as required.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in development studies, environmental science, Social Science, or any other relevant fields. Master’s Degree preferred
  • At least 5 years’ experience of humanitarian/emergency response, recovery and inclusion especially in implementation with a strong background on coordination with multiple stakeholders and humanitarian program management for government, national or international non-government agencies.
  • Experience working in cash transfer modalities including both cash and vouchers, with specific experience and/or knowledge of digital cash transfer options.
  • Experiences working in partnerships; coordination among different stakeholders and organizations at local and provincial levels is required.
  • Good understanding of humanitarian contexts, humanitarian coordination system, humanitarian standard and principles and humanitarian accountability initiatives in Nepal.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in complex environments under tight deadlines.
  • Strong partnership management skills, including capacity to coordinate with teams remotely.
  • Excellent spoken and written English and Nepali language skills and ability to interact effectively with international and national staff.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality humanitarian programs. S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

Reintegration and Economic Mobility through Inclusive Public Employment Services (ReMi) Project, Phase II (subject to the approval of the ReMi Phase II) is a bilateral initiative between the Governments of Nepal and Switzerland. It is implemented by the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment (MoYLE), respective provincial line ministries and participating local governments. The project is funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and Helvetas Nepal provides technical assistance.

Helvetas Nepal invites applications from dynamic and committed Nepali citizens for the following positions (subject to the approval of the ReMi Phase II):

Employment and Reintegration Services Coordinator – 1 position(s) – Open For All

Duty Station: Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment (MoYLE), Singha durbar, Kathmandu

Job Description

Job purpose: The primary purpose of this position is to work closely with MoYLE to support policy, guidelines and procedures that enhance efficient and effective public employment services delivery at Employment, Skills and Entrepreneurship Centers (ESECs) in Nepal, including support for reintegration of returnee migrants. The role aims to strengthen the ESECs across Nepal to ensure its full function and provide holistic and quality services on public employment services, including labour, employment, migration and reintegration. Additionally, it involves contributing to the promotion of productive domestic and foreign employment opportunities while fostering synergies with relevant development partners.

Roles and Responsibilities

Specific roles and responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Coordination, Collaboration and Networking

  • Support MoYLE to organise the thematic committee meeting on labour and employment, public employment services, and digitalization; follow up on the decisions of the committee and ensure that the key related agenda are discussed in the meeting.
  • Enhance inter-ministry coordination and coordinate with government and stakeholders at all levels to strengthen policies, procedures, and guidelines, particularly related to public employment services (including migration and reintegration) and digitalization.
  • Effective coordination and facilitation among various departments, projects (ReMi, SaMi, K-HaMi and other relevant projects), and development partners (SDC, World Bank, ILO, FCDO, KOICA, JICA, ADB) within MoYLE, as well as across provincial and local governments and local-level associations.
  • Enhance program complementarity and strategic coherence with all relevant projects through aligned government strategies, policies, guidelines, communication on public employment services, labour migration and reintegration services.
  • Facilitate aligned support from relevant projects and development partners to MoYLE and the ESECs to improve governance, operations, and financing frameworks of the ESECs.
  • Engage with the Foreign Employment Board, Department of Foreign Employment, and others in planning, monitoring and implementation of integrated public employment services, integration of digital systems and implementation of respective reintegration programs, ensuring that ReMi interventions are aligned and coordinated with all other related programs and projects.
  • Coordinate with all levels of government to establish one door ESEC and digitalization.

2. Technical assistance

  • Review any available research, labour market analyses, the employment services assessments, etc to inform and facilitate policy and programmatic discussion within the Ministry, projects and with development partners.
  • Draw learning and experiences of ReMi project and support MoYLE to incorporate the learning in reintegration, public employment service and private sector related policies, guidelines and programs.
  • Be updated on various inter-governmental regional consultative processes and inform/sensitize senior government officials about the importance of and engagement in such platforms.

3. Institutional and Operational Mechanism to Strengthen ESECs

  • Support MoYLE for coordination and consultation with different divisions, sections and institutions providing reintegration and public employment service to review the service packages of ESECs and support to enhance and clarify the role and responsibilities of ESECs.
  • Support MoYLE to develop and implement capacity building strategy for updated labour, employment, migration, reintegration and public employment services provided through the ESECs including scope of work, resources (human, technical and financial) required, implementation of standard operating procedures, and monitoring and quality assurance frameworks.
  • Support MoYLE in developing and implementing the digitalisation plan related to labour, employment, migration and reintegration in close coordination with digitalization specialist.
  • Identify opportunities for systematic engagement with private sector, the formalization of linkages and referrals with relevant public and private sectors, and the employers’ associations, cooperatives, and other relevant member-based organizations.

4. Coordination support for ReMi Project

  • Work as a facilitator between ReMi project and the MoYLE in coordination with Deputy Team Leader and other ReMi team members.
  • Facilitate communication and collaboration between ReMi PSU team and concerned Ministries/Departments at federal level as required.
  • Facilitate and support MoYLE on planning and budgeting in relation to the project mandate.
  • Extend support on public finance management including planning and reporting.
  • Support the ReMi team by providing policy-related information, facilitation, and timely updates on policy changes and processes at MoYLE and other relevant ministries concerning labor, employment, migration, and reintegration.
  • Support to organize steering/advisory committee meetings and other meetings with MoYLE.

5. Compliance to policies, rules/regulations, and guidelines

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Code of Conduct; NPR-Nepal; Finance Manual; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Guide; Mobbing, Sexual Harassment & Abuse of Authority; Code of Conduct Against Corruption etc.) and other specific policies applicable for ReMi.
  • Ensure Conflict Sensitive Program Management at all levels.
  • Ensure compliance of all the terms and conditions agreed between HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation Nepal and the donor.

6. Other Specific Responsibilities

  • Professionally discharge other mutually agreed tasks assigned by the ReMi Deputy Team Leader.

Job Requirements:

  • A. Minimum Education Attainment: Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Economics, Development Cooperation or in any relevant discipline.
  • B. Minimum Professional Experience: Minimum 5 years of working experience in project/ programme with at least 3 years dedicated experience in governance, public policy development, employment services and private sector engagement. Having experience in labour migration and working with government system is an added value. Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion and poverty reduction; and sensitivity towards migrant workers and their families.

C. Required Competencies:

  • Ability of working in a complex multi-stakeholder project with public institution and systems building objectives.
  • Sound understanding on migration, reintegration and social protection are an added value.
  • Knowledge on project cycle management, including outcome/results-based project implementation, monitoring and reporting.
  • Strong social skills for collaboration with wide variety of stakeholders including three levels of government agencies, national and international development partners, private sector and civil society.
  • Strong understanding on governance system, particularly on the federal context of Nepal.
  • Strong networking skills, ability to link various actors and institutions.
  • Strong communication, negotiation and facilitating skills.
  • Excellent analytical, conceptual and programmatic competencies.
  • Excellent reporting and writing skills.
  • Strong motivator, a team player, and collaborator. .
  • Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, and poverty reduction.
  • Fluency in English and Nepali, both written and orally is essential.
  • Knowledge on digitalization will be an added value.
  • IT: Proficiency in using office application software.

Additional Information

Duration: Initially for 3 years

Salary and Benefits: As per the rules and regulation of Helvetas Nepal.

Application Procedures: Interested candidates who meet above requirements are requested to visit our website at http://apply.helvetasnepal.org and submit application through online portal. Detail job description is available on the website.

Any telephone inquiries and/or attempts to apply undue influence will result disqualification of candidates. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the selection process. Helvetas Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reasons.

Helvetas Nepal promotes workforce diversity and applies positive discrimination to candidates from discriminated groups (Women, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai, and other minority communities).

The Safer Migration (SaMi) Programme is a bilateral initiative of the governments of Nepal and Switzerland. The programme is implemented in partnership between federal, provincial, and local governments. Helvetas Nepal provides technical assistance to the programme on behalf of the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC). We encourage interested Nepali citizens with a keen desire to learn to apply for this Traineeship opportunity.

Posiiton: Trainee
No. of Vacancy: 7
Duty Station: Biratnagar, Janakpur, Hetauda, Pokhara, Surkhet, Dang and Dhangadhi

Job Description

Coach/Mentor: Provincial Program Manager

Key learning objectives: The trainee will gain first-hand knowledge of a professional working environment and acquire skills in the field of migration and development. The trainee will learn about the different phases of migration, as well as the related challenges and prospects. Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Provincial Program Manager, the trainee will have the opportunity to learn about the dynamics of the labour migration sector, project/program cycle management, the Migration Resource Centres (MRCs), Employment Skills and Entrepreneurship Centres (ESEC), federal state building and the role of the three spheres of government and their linkages to the migration sector.

Learning areas

1. Project management and implementation

  • Participate in workshops, dialogues, and trainings on migration/reintegration and foreign employment;
  • Support on program monitoring, review, and reporting;
  • Engage/support to program-related research and evaluation;
  • Support to enhance the program quality of the Migration Resource Center;
  • Support in organizing consultations, workshops, etc., drafting letters and minutes;
  • Support in the development of Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials and social media content;
  • Understand the employment and migration governance-related issues and contribute to the SaMi program; and
  • Learn and follow the Conflict-Sensitive Programme Management at all levels.

2. Federal state-building, planning, and budgeting

  • Support in data management of program components, including migration/ reintegration profile and safer migration/ reintegration guidelines;
  • Provide support in organizing consultation meetings, inter-government coordination meetings, and workshops, etc., and drafting letters and minutes;
  • Understand the role of different governments (Federal, Provincial, and Local) on employment and migration governance and associated issues, and contribute to the SaMi program;
  • Engage and learn by participating in programs on migration related services organized by Local Governments, and
  • Support the program team in coordination with the relevant stakeholders as required.

3. Data Management and Reporting

  • Understand and support data management, data collection, and document best practices;
  • Learn and support in documenting case studies, best practices, program photos, and videos under the program;
  • Support in monitoring of project components based on the monitoring checklist.

4. Others

  • Act proactively in performing the aforesaid tasks;
  • Provide support in other tasks as required and requested; and
  • Have a learning attitude and expand your knowledge and experience in safer migration ecosystems.

5. Compliance with policies, rules/regulations, and guidelines

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations, and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Personnel, Financial, Administrative policies; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social
  • Inclusion Guide; Sexual Harassment & Mobbing Policy; Code of Conduct Against Corruption, etc.) and other specific policies applicable; and
    Compliance with the GoN and SDC policies and approaches as relevant and required.

Eligibility Criteria and Competencies

A. Eligibility Criteria:

  • Bachelor’s degree in the field of social science, humanities, public administration, education, law, health, or any other relevant field.
  • Fresh graduate with no prior job experience. Completion of a bachelor’s degree within two years while applying for the position.
  • Willingness to undertake extensive field travel within and outside the province.
  • Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, poverty reduction, and sensitivity towards migrant workers and their families.
  • Proactive and a keen learning attitude and a sense of responsibility.
  • Woman/man from Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai caste/ethnicity, ethnic and religious minorities, discriminated Newar castes.

B. Competencies Required:

  • Knowledge of labor migration and reintegration of Nepali migrant workers.
  • Willingness and interest in travel to project field locations (70%) within the provinces, and other provinces as well.
  • Eagerness and self-initiation to learn and develop a career in the migration sector.
  • Basic understanding of the functioning of local government and federalism principles and the political context.
  • Reliable, sincere, and having a positive attitude.
  • Excellent time management, task prioritization skills, and result orientation.
  • Polite with good interpersonal and intercultural competencies.
  • Good English & Nepali skills (oral, written, and typing); knowledge of local languages is an advantage.
  • Good facilitation and communication skills, including the ability to represent and interact effectively with different stakeholders.
  • Good team player and effective communicator.

Additional Information

Duration: 1 year (12 months) with a fixed duration.

Local candidates from remote municipalities of the respective province will have an advantage.

Interested and committed fresh graduates are requested to visit our website at https://apply.helvetasnepal.org and submit their application through the online portal. Detailed learning objectives are available on the website.

Group of Helping Hands (SAHAS) Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental organization established in 1996. Since its establishment, SAHAS Nepal has been working with vulnerable and socially excluded communities through social mobilization, grassroots organization building, Community-Based Network Organization (CBNO) formation and capacity development. SAHAS Nepal implements diverse programmes and projects in sustainable agriculture and food security, climate change, education, and related areas across 21 districts of Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal will implement a scholarship project titled “Bridging Futures: Education Access Initiative.” The project aims to support academically qualified young people and civil society actors from disadvantaged and marginalized groups to access higher education, develop their leadership capacities, and contribute to socio-ecological change and sustainable development in their communities and Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal invites applications from energetic, committed, competent, and creative Nepali citizens for the following positions.

Posiiton: Scholarship Coordinator

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Kathmandu, with approximately 60% travel to project locations

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, Management, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in education, scholarship management, youth development, social inclusion, or development projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in project planning, implementation, monitoring, budgeting, reporting, and team coordination.
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s higher education system, education policies, scholarship mechanisms, and relevant government regulations.
  • Strong networking and coordination skills with universities, colleges, government agencies, development partners, and other education stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills in both Nepali and English.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate team members and work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Strong computer skills, including MS Office applications; knowledge of project management and reporting systems will be an advantage.
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently to project locations.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership and Implementation

  • Lead overall implementation of the scholarship project in accordance with project objectives, approved plans, policies, and donor requirements.
  • Develop and regularly update annual, quarterly, and monthly implementation plans.
  • Provide technical and managerial guidance to project team members.

Scholarship Management

  • Lead and oversee the scholarship application, screening, selection, award, and renewal processes in a transparent, inclusive, and accountable manner.
  • Ensure that scholarship implementation complies with approved criteria, project guidelines, and applicable policies.
  • Maintain regular communication with scholars and ensure they understand programme rules, responsibilities, academic requirements, and reporting obligations.

Coordination and Networking

  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with universities, colleges, academic institutions, finance departments, teachers, government authorities, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Liaise with universities and colleges to verify student enrolment, academic progress, fee requirements, and other relevant information.
  • Explore opportunities for institutional collaboration and resource sharing to maximize benefits for scholars.

Financial and Administrative Management

  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and ensure compliance with SAHAS Nepal and donor financial requirements.
  • Contribute to budget revisions, financial forecasting, and preparation of financial and narrative reports.

Monitoring, Reporting and Learning

  • Track project progress against agreed targets and indicators.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor programme effectiveness and identify challenges and areas for improvement.
  • Prepare timely project reports documenting project achievements, good practices, lessons learned, success stories, and challenges.

Posiiton: Admin and Finance Officer

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Kathmandu, with approximately 40% travel outside the Kathmandu Valley

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience, preferably with NGOs/INGOs, development projects scholarship management.
  • Good knowledge of financial accounting, budgeting, procurement, and administrative systems.
  • Strong working knowledge of MS Excel and other MS Office applications.
  • Experience with Money-Works or similar accounting software will be an advantage.
  • Knowledge of donor financial requirements, taxation, Social Security Fund (SSF), audit procedures, and NGO financial compliance will be an advantage.
  • Good organizational, communication, documentation, and record-keeping skills.
  • Willingness to travel outside the Kathmandu Valley is required.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Process and maintain accurate records of tuition payments, scholarships, stipends, allowances, and other payments to scholars and institutions.
  • Maintain proper financial documentation and supporting documents for all project transactions.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and provide regular budget updates.
  • Assist in preparing financial reports in accordance with SAHAS Nepal and funding partner requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational financial policies, donor requirements, applicable tax regulations, and audit requirements.

Administration and Procurement

  • Manage procurement of project supplies, equipment, and services in accordance with organizational procedures.
  • Support Scholarship Coordinator in managing logistics during the events and training programs.
  • Maintain organized physical and digital administrative filing systems.
  • Maintain project asset and stock records and ensure proper safeguarding and utilization of project assets.

Human Resource and Compliance Support

  • Support timely processing of staff salaries and benefits.
  • Assist with internal and external audits by maintaining complete and accessible financial and administrative documentation.

Posiiton: Student Support and Scholarship Outreach Facilitator

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Field

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, Counselling, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum 1 year of relevant professional experience, preferably in education, youth development, scholarship programmes, counselling, or social development.
  • Experience in academic counselling, mentoring, youth engagement, community outreach, or student support will be an advantage.
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s education system, higher education opportunities, and relevant policies.
  • Ability to work with students and young people from diverse and disadvantaged backgrounds.
  • Good computer and documentation skills in both Nepali and English.
  • Willingness to travel to schools, communities, colleges, and other project locations.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, facilitation, mentoring, and networking skills.

Key Responsibilities

Student Support and Mentorship

  • Provide scholars with academic advising, career guidance, mentorship, and regular well-being check-ins.
  • Monitor scholars’ academic progress and identify students who may require additional support.
  • Act as the first point of support when a scholar faces academic, personal, financial, or other challenges that may affect their participation or scholarship eligibility.
  • Maintain appropriate and confidential records of student support and follow-up.

Scholarship Outreach and Recruitment

  • Visit schools, colleges, universities, communities, and other relevant locations to identify and reach potential applicants.
  • Support dissemination of scholarship calls, eligibility criteria, application procedures, and deadlines.

Capacity Building and Networking

  • Develop and maintain networks with schools, colleges, universities, youth groups, community organizations, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Encourage scholars to participate in learning, leadership, community engagement, and professional development opportunities.

Monitoring and Documentation

  • Maintain updated records of scholar participation, academic progress, support provided, and follow-up actions.
  • Contribute to project monitoring, success stories, case studies, and periodic reports.
  • Provide regular feedback to the Scholarship Coordinator on student needs, emerging challenges, and opportunities for improvement.

Salary and Benefits

Salary and benefits will be provided as per the rules and regulations of SAHAS Nepal and based on the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate.

Application Procedure

Interested Nepali citizens are requested to submit the following documents:

1. An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV).
2. A cover letter clearly indicating the position applied for and demonstrating the candidate’s interest and suitability for the position.
3. Mailing address and telephone number.
4. Details of two professional references, including their contact information.

Applications should be submitted to the Executive Director, SAHAS Nepal, by 10th September 2026, via email at: sahasnepalvacancy@gmail.com

Telephone enquiries will not be entertained. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further screening and selection processes.

SAHAS Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reason.

Equal Opportunity, Diversity and Inclusion: SAHAS Nepal promotes workforce diversity and inclusion and applies positive discrimination in favour of candidates from marginalized and disadvantaged groups. Applications from women and members of Indigenous, marginalized, and disadvantaged communities are highly encouraged.

Safeguarding and Zero Tolerance: SAHAS Nepal is committed to safeguarding and maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward abuse, exploitation, corruption, bribery, fraud, sexual harassment, and all forms of misconduct.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Posiiton: Compliance Manager
Location: Kathmandu

Jhpiego is an international, non-profit health organization affiliated with The Johns Hopkins University. For 50 years and in over 155 countries, Jhpiego has worked to prevent the needless deaths of women and their families.

Reporting to the Country Director, the Compliance Manager is accountable for identifying risks that hinder the achievement of Jhpiego’s strategic and program objectives, developing standardized approaches to a reduced risk profile in the country office, and leading communications on all fraud-related issues.  Additionally, this position will participate in the annual risk assessment process in partnership with the country teams to develop strategies and action plans that strengthen Jhpiego’s internal controls and compliance capacity.  Other responsibilities include providing guidance, training, and compliance oversight in the areas of procurement, subrecipient monitoring, financial management, and other operational areas as needed.  The Compliance Manager demonstrates excellent organizational and technical skills and is a dedicated, hardworking, and highly motivated professional. S/he should be an effective team player with an innovative and solution-oriented approach, and is capable of managing multiple priorities and delivering results effectively in high-pressure environments. Duty station being in Dhaka or Kathmandu, the Compliance Manager will oversee compliance functions for Jhpiego Bangladesh and Nepal offices.

Working with the Sr. Compliance Director, Jhpiego’s Bangladesh and Nepal office Leadership/ teams, the Compliance Manager ensures program compliance with applicable policies, guidelines, regulations and procedures.

Location: Asia, with preference for Bangladesh & Nepal

Responsibilities

  • Work with the Country Director(s), Director Compliance, Director Finance, country leadership, and HQ teams to establish, maintain, and strengthen effective internal controls, compliance processes, and risk management systems.
  • Develop and implement an annual compliance monitoring and review plan based on the country office project portfolio, including routine monthly and quarterly reviews, spot checks, field visits, and other compliance activities.
  • Monitor compliance with donor regulations, contractual obligations, organizational policies and procedures, and applicable U.S. , host country, and other relevant laws and regulations.
  • Identify areas of compliance vulnerability and risk; conduct risk assessments and support the development, implementation, and monitoring of corrective action plans.
  • Coordinate the organization’s risk management framework and actively work with management to identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor operational, financial, compliance, and programmatic risks.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain effective subrecipient monitoring and oversight systems in accordance with JHU and Jhpiego policies, including monitoring visits, compliance audits, and follow-up on corrective actions.
  • Work with the Finance Director (s) to support external audits, donor reviews, Johns Hopkins University (JHU) audits, and other compliance assessments, and support management in responding to audit findings and implementing recommendations.
  • Track, monitor, and regularly report on the implementation status of audit findings, compliance recommendations, and management action plans to senior leadership.
  • Support the Finance team in review process and other internal control assessments as needed.
  • Prepare and present compliance review reports, risk assessments, and management updates to senior leadership.
  • Develop, deliver, and coordinate compliance and ethics training programs; assess staff training needs and promote awareness of applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Provide tools, and guidance to staff and support their implementation across the organization.
  • Maintain and promote an effective compliance and ethics program, including serving as a confidential point of contact for reporting compliance concerns, misconduct, or irregularities.
  • Conduct compliance investigations, special reviews, analytical assignments, and other projects as requested by management.
  • Immediately escalate suspected fraud, gross misconduct, or other significant compliance concerns in accordance with organizational reporting requirements.
  • Collaborate with the global compliance team to review and improve policies, procedures, monitoring tools, templates, and best practices.
  • Participate in Internal Compliance Reviews (ICRs), regional compliance initiatives, and other compliance-related assignments as required.
  • Maintain current knowledge of relevant donor requirements, regulatory developments, compliance standards, and industry best practices.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Postgraduate qualification in a business-related field is an added advantage.
  • Professional certification such as ACCA, CIA, CISA, CPA, or equivalent, with membership in a relevant professional body preferred.
  • Minimum 7-8 years of progressively responsible experience in audit, accounting, compliance, risk management, or internal controls, preferably within an international NGO environment, including at least 2 years in a supervisory or management role.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles, auditing standards, internal controls, risk management practices, and compliance frameworks.
  • Demonstrated understanding of donor regulations and compliance requirements, particularly those of the S. Government, Gates Foundation, and other major institutional donors.
  • Good understanding of internal audit methodologies, emerging trends, and international best practices.

Position: Humanitarian Response Officer

Required Number: 1 position

Duty Station: Dhading with frequent travel to Nuwakot

Duration: 4 months with possibility of extension based on response needs, performance, and availability of funding.

In response to recent flash flood in Rasuwa, across Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan, DCA Nepal is supporting the government in relief distribution for affected communities, providing emergency relief to families who have lost their homes and belongings. As an initial response, we are distributing essential items to the affected community particularly at Dhading and Nuwakot in coordination with our local partner, as well as all relevant local authorities and other humanitarian organisations.

In this context, DCA is seeking to recruit Humanitarian Response Officer, who will be responsible to coordinate the efforts of humanitarian response works at Dhading and Nuwakot District. S/he will support the planning, implementation, monitoring and coordination work with the district and Palika level offices working closely with partners, and other relevant stakeholders. S/he will be responsible for day-to-day operational coordination and implementation of the response activity, including needs assessments, community and beneficiary identification, activity planning, field implementation, distribution, feedback and monitoring, coordination with local authorities and humanitarian actors maintaining strong data management and operational reporting.

This is a field-oriented position based at Dhading but regular visit to Nuwakot. Under the supervision of DCA Program Manager with agreed plans and delegated authority, s/he is expected to escalate strategic, safeguarding, donor and budget decisions to Crisis Management Team. S/he works closely with the Crisis Management Team to ensure that assistance is delivered rapidly, appropriately and transparently, in accordance with DCA procedures, humanitarian principles and donor requirements.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and facilitate DCA humanitarian response activities at the district and palika level, including planning, distribution, implementation, monitoring, follow-up, and coordination of response interventions targeting affected and vulnerable populations.
  • Coordinate with local government, partners, other stakeholders and DCA teams to ensure continuity and timely delivery of relief items, cash assistance, and early recovery activities
  • Constant communication and coordination with Focal Persons of DPNet deployed at Nuwakot for related information-management support.
  • Support government bodies in the districts and palikas to manage program and emergency response data by coordinating data collection from the community and identifying beneficiaries ensuring data quality and accuracy, maintaining databases and records, and preparing regular summaries and reports
  • Maintain regular communication with affected communities, ensuring transparent beneficiary verification and support accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms and promptly escalate serious or unresolved concerns.
  • Collect and provide required information to DCA team related to relief distribution, or planning in order to report and complete respective cluster activity reporting in addition to the existing SWC obligation
  • Monitor and document response activities and emerging needs, identify implementation gaps, and provide timely updates and recommendations to the DCA team to support effective decision-making and adaptive response.
  • Provide coordination and technical support to government authorities within the scope of work, including participation in coordination meetings, information sharing, joint planning, and other response-related activities as required.
  • Support DCA team in joint needs assessment- together with other NGOs, in partnership with DPNet – to guide the early recovery and future interventions.
  • Participate in clusters, sector meetings, working groups, joint assessments or other humanitarian coordination mechanisms at district level when requested or delegated
  • Represent DCA professionally at district level when specifically delegated, while referring safeguarding, high-level institutional and donor matters to Crisis Management Team
  • Maintain accurate records of relief distribution, beneficiary registries, and partner activity for accountability and reporting purposes
  • Support partners in implementing accountability mechanisms (feedback/complaints, community consultation) in line with CHS commitments
  • Contribute to concept note and proposal development for emergency and early recovery funding
  • Ensure protection, gender, and inclusion considerations are integrated into response activities, prioritizing vulnerable groups (women, children, elderly, PWD)
  • Other related tasks as assigned by the line manager

Required Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master’s degree in development studies, Rural Development, Social Science, Disaster risk management and Natural Resource Management with 3 years of work experience with an I/NGO or development organization. Preference will be given to Disaster Risk Management.
  • Demonstrated experience in emergencies, working with local government structures (DDMC/DAO), clusters, and INGO/NGO coordination mechanisms
  • Prior experience in cash-based programming, NFI/shelter distribution, or early recovery activities is an advantage
  • Proven experience in data management, analysis, documentation, and reporting.
  • Good interpersonal, active listening, and communication skills, with cultural sensitivity, professionalism, and the ability to remain calm under pressure.
  • Ability to work effectively in challenging field conditions and flexible working hours, while maintaining personal resilience and well-being.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to and stay in disaster-affected and remote areas as required.

​Location: Rasuwa, Nuwakot or Dhading, Nepal

Contract Type: Fixed term
Contract Duration: Till February 2027
