About CBM Global

CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

  • Break the cycle of poverty and disability
  • Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
  • Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

About the Role

​
CBM Global Nepal has initiated a humanitarian response in areas affected by the devastating flash floods in the Bhotekoshi River and downstream river systems. The response covers affected communities in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts and focuses on mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), basic needs assistance, provision of assistive devices, rehabilitation services, and advocacy and technical support to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the overall humanitarian response.

The Humanitarian Response Project Officer will be responsible for coordinating humanitarian response interventions in close collaboration with partner organizations. The position provides overall oversight of project implementation, including partner support, budget management, monitoring, documentation, and reporting. S/he will serve as the focal point for project implementation with partners and stakeholders on behalf of CBM Global Nepal.

​

Key Responsibilities

​​

A. Project Implementation Oversight

​

  • ​Guide and support the implementation of humanitarian response activities in accordance with the project plans, budgets, and timelines.
  • Oversee coordination among partners to ensure coherent and effective implementation.
  • Ensure strong coordination and collaboration with project stakeholders, including Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), local governments, cluster mechanisms, and other humanitarian stakeholders.
  • Ensure project interventions adhere to quality standards, humanitarian principles, and organizational policies.
  • Monitor activities and resource utilization to ensure efficiency, effectiveness, and value for money.
  • Manage project finances in close coordination with the finance team
  • Identify implementation challenges, risks, and bottlenecks, and propose appropriate mitigation measures.
  • Support rapid and ongoing needs assessments, identify emerging humanitarian needs and recommend timely adaptations to response activities.
    ​

B. Partner Coordination and Support

​

  • Manage partner relations and maintain close collaboration with all project partners.
  • Ensure partners understand project objectives, donor requirements, and expected results.
  • Facilitate regular coordination meetings with partners to review progress, address challenges, and ensure timely implementation.
  • Participate in technical meetings with local authorities, clusters, NGOs, and relevant institutions, and share key updates with the line manager.
  • Serve as the primary focal point for partners on behalf of CBM Global Nepal.
    ​

C. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

​

  • Conduct regular monitoring visits to project sites to ensure quality implementation and achievement of project objectives.
  • Track project indicators and maintain accurate project records and databases.
  • Generate evidence through systematic documentation of best practices, lessons learned, success stories, and case studies.
  • Coordinate the preparation and submission of high-quality reports in a timely manner.
  • Support partners in data collection, analysis, and reporting processes.
  • Support partners to establish and implement inclusive, accessible, and effective feedback, complaints, and response mechanisms (FCRM), ensuring meaningful participation of persons with disabilities.
    ​

F. Safeguarding

​

​Knowledge

Understands the incident management framework and their first responder role in recording, responding and reporting incidents.

Understands the survivor-centered approach and how to apply it when receiving a complaint or responding to an incident. Knows local support services available in the community or region, and how to engage them.

Skills

Able to listen and accurately document reported concerns and complaints. Able to respect the confidentiality of safeguarding allegations. Able to appropriately apply the survivor-centred approach.

Behaviours

Treats the survivor and others involved in an incident with dignity and respect.

Be assertive in implementing the initial incident response protocols by gaining the trust and cooperation of parties involved.
​

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for a candidate who brings the following experience and qualities:

All the following requirements are Essential, unless marked with a * when they are Desirable.

Experience and Knowledge

​

  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in managing development and/or humanitarian projects in I/NGOs.
  • Experience in managing disability inclusive humanitarian response or recovery projects/ programmes preferred.*
  • Experience working simultaneously with multiple partners.
  • Experience working with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) preferred.*
  • Experience engaging with local government systems, humanitarian clusters, and development partners.
  • Demonstrated experience in reporting, documentation, and knowledge management.
  • Proven experience in project financial management.
    ​

Skills/Competencies/Personal Qualities

​

  • Strong knowledge of humanitarian principles and coordination mechanisms.
  • Excellent coordination and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong planning and organizational abilities with a results-oriented approach.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing work demands in emergency contexts.
  • Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and respond to dynamic environments.
  • Knowledge of disability inclusion principles.*
  • Strong communication skills in English (oral and written).
  • Alignment to CBM Global values (Our Vision, Mission and Values | CBM Global) and Safeguarding Policy (CBM-Global-Policy-Safeguarding.pdf) and Code of Conduct (CBM-Global-Code-of-Conduct.pdf)
    ​

Qualifications

​

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Disaster Risk Management, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred*.
    ​

We welcome and encourage applications from people with lived experience of disability.

​

We proactively work on achieving a diverse and inclusive work environment for people from all backgrounds and abilities.

​

Why work with Us?

​

  • A chance to be part of a global movement pursuing an inclusive world for people with disabilities.
  • A supportive, flexible, and inclusive work environment.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • A culture that champions Mental Health and Wellbeing.
  • Opportunities for learning, growth, and international collaboration.
  • Competitive remuneration and benefits.

Hear from our colleagues

We are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive People Operations Executive to support and manage the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of the People & Culture department.

The role will be responsible for maintaining accurate employee records, supporting onboarding and offboarding processes, coordinating attendance and payroll inputs, handling employee queries, maintaining People & Culture documentation, and supporting statutory compliance and audits.

The ideal candidate should be organized, dependable, and capable of independently managing routine People Operations activities with minimal supervision while maintaining confidentiality, accuracy, and compliance with company policies and applicable statutory requirements.

Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Management, or a related field.
  • 1–2 years of relevant experience in People Operations, or a similar role.
  • Working knowledge of employee lifecycle processes, HR administration, payroll coordination, and statutory compliance.
  • Knowledge of Labor Act, SSF, and other applicable employment-related requirements.
  • Prior experience supporting internal or external audits will be an advantage.
  • Familiarity with HRIS platforms is preferred.

Job Description

People Operations & HRIS

  • Maintain and regularly update accurate employee records in the HRIS.
  • Ensure proper filing, documentation, and maintenance of People & Culture records in accordance with company policies and statutory requirements.
  • Maintain an updated repository of employee policies, procedures, and People & Culture by-laws.
  • Prepare employment contracts, offer letters, experience letters, relieving letters, and other People & Culture-related documents.

Onboarding & Offboarding

  • Coordinate the employee onboarding process, including preparation of induction materials and completion of required documentation.
  • Ensure timely completion and filing of new hire documentation.
  • Manage employee exit formalities, including clearance, documentation, and full & final settlement coordination.
  • Issue experience and relieving letters and support the scheduling and coordination of exit interviews.

Attendance, Leave & Payroll Support

  • Monitor and maintain employee attendance and leave records.
  • Process leave applications and ensure timely updates in the HRIS.
  • Generate attendance and leave reports as required.
  • Collect, verify, and submit payroll inputs, including attendance, leave, and other relevant employee information.
  • Coordinate with Finance/Payroll to ensure payroll inputs and documentation are accurate and submitted on time.
  • Verify employee benefit claims and coordinate with relevant departments for processing.
  • Support timely completion of payroll-related documentation and reconciliations.

Compliance & Audit

  • Support compliance with applicable labor laws, including the Labor Act, Social Security Fund (SSF) requirements, and other statutory requirements.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date statutory and People & Culture documentation.
  • Assist in preparing documents, records, reports, and supporting evidence required for internal and external audits.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments to gather information and documentation required during audits.
  • Ensure employee records, contracts, attendance, leave, payroll-related documents, and other People & Culture records are properly maintained and audit-ready.
  • Track audit observations, support corrective actions, and maintain proper documentation of compliance activities.
  • Assist in identifying documentation gaps and follow up with relevant stakeholders for timely closure.
  • Ensure People & Culture processes and records are aligned with company policies and applicable statutory requirements.

Employee Support & Query Management

  • Act as the first point of contact for routine employee queries related to policies, leave, attendance, benefits, documentation, and People Operations processes.

Swisscontact, established in 1959 in Switzerland, is a leading partner organisation for the implementation of international development projects. The organisation promotes inclusive economic, social, and ecological development to make an effective contribution towards sustainable and widespread prosperity in developing and emerging economies. It strengthens the competencies of people, improving their employability, increases the competitiveness of enterprises, growing their business, and fosters social and economic systems, promoting inclusive development.

Swisscontact, registered as an International Non-Governmental Organisation in Nepal, has been operating in Nepal since 1991. Currently, Swisscontact in Nepal has six development programmes across all seven provinces.

The Municipal Revenue Enhancement Project (MunRev) is a bilateral initiative of the Governments of Nepal and Switzerland, implemented by the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoLMCFAGA) and selected 12 partner municipalities of Koshi and Bagmati Provinces, with technical assistance from Swisscontact in Nepal. MunRev supports local governments to strengthen own-source revenue and tax compliance, improve inclusive and transparent public service delivery, and foster cross-government learning for better-informed fiscal policy, with gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) mainstreamed throughout. Through these efforts, the project aims to enhance the fiscal capacity of local governments and improve services for all citizens, including women and disadvantaged groups.

title.rendered: Social Mobilizer, Assistant Logistics Officer, Support Staff (Office Assistant), MEAL Officer, Admin and Finance Officer, Program Officer, Sub-Overseer, Program Coordinator, Civil Engineer, Volunteer/ Enumerator

content.rendered:
Bagmati Welfare Society Nepal (BWSN) is a women-led and youth-led feminist organization established in 1995 in Sarlahi, Nepal. For thirty two years BWSN has worked in the districts where public systems arrived last, and currently works across 201 local levels in Madhesh, Koshi, Lumbini, Karnali and Bagmati Provinces. Its work is organized around three pillars — People, Planet and Power: human wellbeing and social development, climate resilience and biodiversity, and inclusive governance and civic engagement.

The Response

On 26 August 2026, an ice-rock collapse near the Nepal–China border blocked the Lhende Khola. The lake that formed behind the blockage breached and sent a flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. There was no rainfall and no warning, and the Syabrubesi gauging station was destroyed in the flood. The Government of Nepal has declared 15 local levels across five districts disaster crisis-hit for three months under Section 32(1) of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074.

BWSN deployed a response team within hours and coordinated the response from Nuwakot. BWSN is working alongside rural municipalities, municipalities and district authorities on needs assessment, beneficiary identification, delivery and follow-up.

BWSN invites applications from qualified and committed Nepali candidates for the following positions.

Duty Stations: Nuwakot, Dhading and Rasuwa Districts, Bagmati Province

Positions Available

  • Program Coordinator
  • Admin and Finance Officer
  • Civil Engineer
  • Sub-Overseer
  • Program Officer
  • Social Mobilizer
  • Psychosocial Support (PSS) Coordinator
  • Psychosocial Counsellor
  • Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer
  • MEAL Officer
  • Assistant Logistics Officer
  • Support Staff (Office Assistant)
  • Volunteer/ Enumerator

Position Descriptions

1. Program Coordinator

Key responsibilities

  • Lead rapid and follow-up WASH assessments in flood-affected wards and displacement sites, working through ward offices and municipal WASH focal points rather than conducting parallel assessments.
  • Plan and oversee emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene interventions, including restoration of damaged water points, water treatment and safe storage, emergency latrines and solid waste management.
  • Represent BWSN in the district WASH Cluster and in municipal coordination meetings in Bidur, Tarkeshwor and Rasuwa, and ensure BWSN’s planned coverage is registered with local government to avoid duplication and gaps.
  • Agree WASH beneficiary lists with rural municipality and municipality officials under the one-door system, and ensure BWSN activity is recorded in local government reporting.
  • Ensure interventions meet Sphere and national WASH standards, and monitor water quality and public health risk, including acute watery diarrhoea and other outbreak risk in displacement sites.
  • Supervise WASH-related work of Social Mobilizers, volunteers, contractors and suppliers, and verify quality of delivered works and materials.
  • Prepare WASH technical specifications, work plans, budgets, activity reports and inputs to donor reporting.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in water supply and Sanitation, Public Health, Environmental Science or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of relevant professional experience, of which at least one year in emergency or humanitarian WASH programming.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating with local government and cluster mechanisms in Nepal.
  • Working knowledge of Sphere standards and national WASH design norms.

2. Admin and Finance Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Manage day-to-day financial transactions of the response, including field advances, cash handling in locations without banking access and timely settlement of advances.
  • Maintain complete accounting records, vouchers, ledgers and supporting documentation for every distribution, procurement and payment.
  • Run procurement in line with BWSN policy and donor requirements, including quotation, comparison, approval and contracting records under emergency provisions.
  • Prepare and monitor budgets, track expenditure against the approved budget, and flag variances and funding gaps to the Program Coordinator early.
  • Maintain the documentation that demonstrates relief delivered through local government has been properly accounted for, including handover and receipt records.
  • Handle personnel administration for the field team, including attendance, leave records, contracts, insurance and orientation documentation.
  • Maintain office and asset records, agreements, and the response filing system in both hard and soft copy.
  • Prepare periodic financial reports and inputs to donor financial reporting, internal review and external audit.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in management, Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience, preferably with NGOs, INGOs or donor-funded projects.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and strong Microsoft Excel skills.
  • High standard of integrity, confidentiality and attention to detail.

3. Civil Engineer

Key responsibilities

  • Support emergency flood response and recovery activities in affected communities and field locations.
  • Conduct rapid assessment of damaged houses, roads, bridges, water systems, and other infrastructure.
  • Collect, verify, and document technical and damage assessment data from affected areas.
  • Support the preparation of site assessments, measurements, BOQs, cost estimates, and technical reports.
  • Provide technical support for repair, rehabilitation, and reconstruction of community infrastructure.
  • Monitor construction and repair works to ensure compliance with approved designs, specifications, quality, and safety standards.
  • Coordinate with contractors, local authorities, community representatives, and field teams during implementation.
  • Support the identification of priority infrastructure needs and emergency rehabilitation requirements.
  • Maintain accurate records of site visits, measurements, photographs, progress, materials, and technical documentation.
  • Provide regular updates on progress, challenges, quality issues, and technical gaps to the Program Coordinator.
  • Perform other technical and emergency response duties assigned by the organization.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelors in Civil Engineering or equivalent; registration with the Nepal Engineering Council is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant site supervision experience; experience in rural water supply, sanitation or post-disaster reconstruction is preferred.
  • Ability to prepare estimates and use relevant design and drawing software.
  • Willingness to work at field sites daily in difficult terrain.

4. Sub-Overseer

Key responsibilities

  • Carry out technical assessment of damaged water supply systems, water points, sanitation facilities and small community infrastructure in the affected wards.
  • Prepare drawings, estimates, bills of quantity and technical specifications for repair and emergency construction works.
  • Supervise construction and repair works on site, including water source protection, pipeline and tap stand repair, emergency latrines and drainage.
  • Verify quality and quantity of materials delivered and works completed and certify measurement books and running bills before payment.
  • Coordinate technical planning with the municipal or rural municipality technical section and ward offices so that works align with local government plans.
  • Ensure works are safe, accessible and usable by women, children, older persons and persons with disabilities.
  • Maintain site records, progress reports, photographs and completion documentation.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering (Overseer level) or equivalent; registration with the Nepal Engineering Council is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant site supervision experience; experience in rural water supply, sanitation or post-disaster reconstruction is preferred.
  • Ability to prepare estimates and use relevant design and drawing software.
  • Willingness to work at field sites daily in difficult terrain.

5. Program Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Support day-to-day implementation of response activities and translate the workplan into weekly and daily field plans.
  • Organise assessments, beneficiary identification, verification and distribution activities in coordination with ward offices and local government.
  • Supervise and support Social Mobilizers in the field, and ensure activities reach the households identified as most at risk.
  • Facilitate coordination meetings at ward and municipal level and maintain working relationships with local officials, community leaders and other agencies.
  • Ensure hygiene promotion, protection messaging and referral information reach affected communities through the field team.
  • Compile field data, activity records and photographs, and prepare activity reports for the Program Coordinator.
  • Support accountability to affected populations, including communication of entitlements, selection criteria and how to raise a complaint.
  • Deputise for the Program Coordinator on specific tasks as delegated.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Development Studies, Public Health, Sociology or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant field implementation experience; emergency response experience is preferred.
  • Good written and spoken English and strong report-writing ability.
  • Experience supervising field-level staff or volunteers.

6. Social Mobilizer

Key responsibilities

  • Work at ward level with ward chairpersons, ward secretaries, tole committees and local groups to support needs assessment and household identification.
  • Support verification of beneficiary lists prepared by the local government, and raise omissions, duplications and exclusion of vulnerable households with the ward office and the BWSN team.
  • Facilitate community meetings and awareness sessions on hygiene, safe water, sanitation, available services and how to raise a complaint.
  • Ensure women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, single women, pregnant and lactating women, and socially excluded households are reached and able to participate.
  • Identify and refer individuals needing psychosocial, protection, health or specialised support to the relevant service provider, and follow up on referrals made.
  • Collect community feedback and complaints and pass them to the MEAL Officer for logging and follow-up.
  • Support distribution days, including crowd and queue management, verification at the point of distribution, and follow-up with households unable to attend.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level; a bachelor’s degree in social work, Sociology, Development Studies, Education or a related field is an advantage.
  • Minimum 1–2 years of community mobilisation experience; experience in emergency response is preferred.
  • Fluency in Nepali; knowledge of Tamang or other local languages spoken in Nuwakot and Rasuwa is a strong advantage.
  • Candidates from the affected wards and districts are particularly encouraged to apply.

7. Psychosocial Support (PSS) Coordinator

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of community-based mental health and psychosocial support activities across the response area.
  • Coordinate rapid identification of psychosocial needs among children, adolescents, adults, older persons and bereaved households, including those who lost family members or homes in the flood.
  • Establish safe, private and confidential spaces for individual and group support in displacement sites and host communities, in agreement with the local government and site management.
  • Supervise and provide technical support and regular case discussion to Psychosocial Counsellors and community-based psychosocial workers.
  • Map and maintain referral pathways to district hospitals, mental health services, the One-Stop Crisis Management Centre, police and protection actors, and agree these pathways with the district authorities.
  • Represent BWSN in protection and MHPSS coordination at district level and with the local government.
  • Ensure PSS activity follows ethical, confidential, person-centred, survivor-centred and Do No Harm principles, and that no case information is shared outside agreed referral protocols.
  • Organise staff care and peer support for BWSN staff and volunteers working in response, and monitor and report on PSS activity.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in psychology, Counselling Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Social Work or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of relevant experience, preferably including humanitarian or emergency settings.
  • Training and practical experience in Psychological First Aid, trauma-informed approaches and community-based MHPSS.
  • Demonstrated supervision experience.

8. Psychosocial Counsellor

Key responsibilities

  • Provide individual and group psychosocial support and basic counselling to flood-affected individuals in displacement sites and host communities.
  • Provide Psychological First Aid to people in acute distress, including those bereaved, displaced or separated from family members.
  • Identify people requiring specialized mental health, medical or protection support and make safe, consented referrals through the agreed pathways.
  • Facilitate awareness sessions on stress, grief, coping and available services, adapted for children, adolescents and adults.
  • Support child-friendly and community-based psychosocial activities in coordination with the Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer.
  • Maintain confidential, accurate and minimal case documentation in line with BWSN data protection requirements.
  • Report caseload patterns and emerging concerns to the PSS Coordinator, without disclosing identifying information beyond agreed protocols.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in psychology, Counselling, Social Work or a related field.
  • Minimum 2 years of counselling or psychosocial support experience is preferred.
  • Training in Psychological First Aid, trauma-informed care or humanitarian MHPSS is an advantage.
  • Ability to work sensitively with people who have experienced sudden loss and displacement.

9. Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Lead child protection and safeguarding work across the response, including risk identification in displacement sites, distribution points and host communities.
  • Identify protection risks affecting children, including family separation, unaccompanied and separated children, child labour, trafficking risk, early marriage, violence, exploitation and neglect.
  • Work with the local government, Nepal Police, the Municipal Child Rights Committee and protection actors on identification, family tracing and case referral for unaccompanied and separated children.
  • Establish and maintain safe referral pathways for children and families requiring specialized services and agree with district authorities.
  • Review distribution and activity plans for child safety and accessibility and advise on changes where activities create risk.
  • Deliver safeguarding, PSEA and Code of Conduct orientation to BWSN staff, volunteers, contractors and, where relevant, community members and local government partners.
  • Ensure safeguarding and PSEA reporting channels are known, accessible and functioning, and that reports are handled confidentially and escalated according to BWSN policy.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, Psychology, Sociology, Child Development, Law, Development Studies or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in child protection, safeguarding or protection programming, including in emergency settings.
  • Working knowledge of Nepal’s child protection framework, PSEA standards and referral mechanisms.
  • Experience delivering safeguarding orientation and handling sensitive reports.

10. MEAL Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Set up and run the MEAL system for the response, including assessment tools, beneficiary tracking, distribution and post-distribution monitoring formats and reporting templates.
  • Reconcile BWSN beneficiary records with local government lists prepared under the one-door system, and document how selection decisions were made and by whom.
  • Carry out field monitoring and post-distribution monitoring in Nuwakot and Rasuwa, including verification visits to households recorded as assisted.
  • Establish and manage the Community Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism, ensure complaints are logged, routed and closed, and report trends to the response team.
  • Prepare situation reports, dashboards and figures for donor and government reporting, using NDRRMA and district figures as the reference source for caseload data.
  • Document lessons learned, adaptations and good practice through the response, including what worked and did not work in coordination with local government.
  • Ensure all data is collected, stored and shared ethically and confidentially, with particular care for protection and psychosocial case data.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Health, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant MEAL or M&E experience, preferably including humanitarian or emergency response.
  • Working proficiency in Kobo Toolbox or ODK and in Microsoft Excel, including data cleaning and basic analysis.
  • Ability to produce clear written analysis in English.

11. Assistant Logistics Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Manage receipt, storage, stock recording and dispatch of relief materials, including items released from the BWSN warehouse and procured locally.
  • Maintain bin cards, stock ledgers, goods received notes, waybills and distribution handover records, and reconcile physical stock with records regularly.
  • Arrange transport to field sites, including in areas where access is by alternative routes, on foot or by porter, and plan loading and offloading.
  • Support procurement by collecting quotations, checking specifications and verifying deliveries against purchase orders.
  • Arrange logistics for distribution days, including site setup, storage at the point of distribution and return of unissued stock.
  • Support fleet, fuel and travel arrangements for the field team and maintain related records.
  • Report stock levels, losses, damage and pipeline gaps to the Admin and Finance Officer and Program Coordinator.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level; a bachelor’s degree in management or a related field is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in logistics, storekeeping or supply chain, preferably with NGOs or in humanitarian operations.
  • Practical experience of warehouse and stock documentation.
  • A valid two-wheeler driving license is an advantage.

12. Volunteers/Enumerators

Key responsibilities

  • Support emergency flood response activities in affected communities and field locations.
  • Assist in the collection, verification, and recording of beneficiary and household data.
  • Conduct field-level data collection and needs assessments from flood-affected communities.
  • Enter and maintain accurate data in Excel, databases, or other reporting systems.
  • Support the preparation and updating of beneficiary lists, distribution records, and field reports.
  • Assist the team in identifying and documenting priority needs, damages, and gaps during the emergency response.
  • Support the distribution of relief materials and maintain related records.
  • Collect and organize information, photos, forms, and other field documentation as required.
  • Coordinate with field teams and community representatives to ensure accurate and timely information collection.
  • Perform other emergency response and administrative tasks assigned by the Program Coordinator or Admin and Finance Officer.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level.
  • Experiences in data collection, data entry, volunteer, preferably with NGOs or in humanitarian operations.
  • A valid two-wheeler driving license is an advantage.
  • Strong and good communication skills.

General Requirements for All Positions

The following apply to every position advertised above and are not repeated in the individual descriptions.

  • Commitment to humanitarian principles, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding and inclusion.
  • Ability to work in a coordination-led response in which BWSN supports and works through local government rather than delivering independently.
  • Fluency in written and spoken Nepali. Good written and spoken English is required for the Program Coordinator, Program Officer, MEAL, Admin and Finance, PSS Coordinator and Child Protection positions.
  • Ability to work in high-pressure conditions with long hours, shifting priorities and incomplete information.
  • Good communication, teamwork and coordination skills, and the ability to work respectfully with local government, communities, other agencies and security forces.
  • Commitment to gender equality, disability inclusion and the protection of vulnerable groups.
  • Nepali citizenship and a valid citizenship certificate.

Safeguarding and Code of Conduct

BWSN maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, child abuse, discrimination, fraud and other misconduct. Duties and Responsibilities

BACKGROUND:

The International Trade Centre (ITC) is the joint agency of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the United Nations (UN). It is the only multilateral organization fully dedicated to supporting the internationalization and competitiveness of small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). ITC’s mission is to foster inclusive and sustainable economic growth through trade and international business development. Through its projects and programmes, ITC contributes to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and advances the global Aid for Trade agenda. ITC is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland (www.intracen.org). ITC is seeking a Team Leader for the Trade Facilitation Programme for South Asia, a four-year regional programme implemented by ITC and funded by the European Union. The programme covers Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka and aims to strengthen the capacity of institutions and businesses across South Asia to better understand, utilise and comply with requirements governing access to the European Union market. The overall objective of the programme is to leverage trade as a driver of sustainable development, poverty reduction and more inclusive socio-economic outcomes. Its specific objective is to enhance the readiness of South Asian institutions and SMEs to understand, utilise and comply with EU market-access requirements. The programme is structured around three key Outputs:

  •  Output 1: Strengthened capacity to interpret and effectively utilise EU preferential trading arrangements, including Everything But Arms (EBA), the Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP) and GSP+.
  •  Output 2: Enhanced preparedness to comply with EU environmental sustainability-related trade legislation and requirements, including those linked to the European Green Deal.
  •  Output 3: Strengthened awareness and capacities to address EU legislation and standards related to corporate sustainability due diligence, labour rights and gender equality. Through these interventions, the programme will support public institutions, business support organisations and private-sector actors in priority sectors and value chains to strengthen regulatory readiness, improve market-access capabilities and respond to evolving EU sustainability and due-diligence requirements. It will also promote regional and country-level cooperation, contribute to business linkages and more sustainable and resilient value chains between South Asia and the European Union. The position is located within ITC’s Office for Asia and the Pacific (OAP). The Team Leader will be based in the programme office in Kathmandu, Nepal, and will lead the day-to-day coordination and implementation of the regional programme in close collaboration with ITC headquarters, country teams, technical units, EU Delegations – particularly the EU Delegation to Nepal which is leading this programme for the EU – and national and regional stakeholders. RESPONSIBILITIES: Under the general guidance of the Chief of OAP and the direct supervision of Project Manager, OAP, both based in Geneva, Switzerland, the Regional Team Leader will be responsible for the following duties: Partner and Client Relationship Management and Project Outreach:
  • Engage tactfully, develop partnerships and manage relationships with the relevant government counterparts and project partners and beneficiaries, maintaining constant liaison, information sharing and communication, obtaining support for project implementation, ensuring commitment and ownership.
  •  Maintain close working-level coordination with the Delegation of the European Union to Nepal in coordination with the Project Manager; Support and coordinate engagement with national and regional stakeholders across Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, including government institutions, business support organisations, sector associations and private-sector representatives.
  • Facilitate interactions, exchanges and cooperation among project stakeholders, including between the public and private sectors.
  •  Represent the project and deliver presentations and interventions at national and regional events and meetings.
  • Identify and manage linkages and synergies with other programmes and initiatives in the region, including those funded by the EU and other development partners Project Implementation, Monitoring, and Reporting:
  •  Coordinate and monitor the day-to-day implementation of project activities and events within the South Asia region and as per agreed workplans.
  •  Ensure operational synergies between and across activities, outputs and stakeholders, with due consideration to beneficiaries’ needs and expectations, skills transfer and exchange of best practices.
  •  Keep detailed track of progress of project activities, prepare and provide updates on status and progress to ITC HQ, and as required to project stakeholders and partners.
  • During the inception phase, support country and stakeholder consultations, validation and prioritisation of sectors/value chains and interventions, identification of implementation partners and beneficiaries, and identification of appropriate quick-win/early activities.
  • Coordinate the preparation and review of annual project workplans, in close consultation with the Project Manager, technical experts and EU Delegations and relevant national/regional stakeholders, as appropriate, for approval by project governance bodies.
  •  Coordinate project monitoring and reporting against the project logical framework, assessment and evaluation missions, in close coordination with the M&E Expert and ITC Project Manager
  •  Contribute to the drafting of result-based project progress reports for governance bodies, produce and submit monthly reports to ITC HQ.
  •  Identify risks to project implementation and propose mitigation actions, discuss and agree on them with ITC HQ and project partners.
  •  Manage the ITC project office in Kathmandu and organize regular team meetings, provide guidance for the work of the experts, attend and contribute to project management meetings led by the Project Manager and involving the whole project team. Support for Project Governance:
  •  Organize the meetings of project governance bodies, including Project Steering Committee (PSC) and Consultative Group meetings and other meetings as relevant (incl. planning the meetings with project partners, devising meeting contents, preparing agendas and notice of meetings, preparing and undertaking presentations).
  •  Support the development and operationalisation of the Terms of Reference, membership and working arrangements of the PSC and Consultative Group.
  •  Make the necessary follow-ups on the adoption/implementation of the recommendations/inputs provided by project governance bodies, in liaison with the project team in ITC HQ. NOTE – The selected candidate must be available for regular duty travel within the participating South Asian countries and, where required, to ITC headquarters and other locations relevant to programme implementation. Copyright: The personnel has to ensure that s/he has obtained the necessary permissions with regard to intellectual property rights required to perform his/her services under this consultancy contract and for the subsequent dissemination by ITC in any form. Documentary proof is to be submitted to ITC. Should any license fee be due for the use of copyrighted materials of third parties, the Consultant shall request the prior written permission from ITC. S/he has further to ensure to obtain accreditation to event(s), if required.

Qualifications/special skills

EDUCATION:

  • An advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in International Trade, Economics, Business Administration, Development Studies, or related field.
  • A first-level degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in the specified fields of studies with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

EXPERIENCE:

  • A minimum of seven (7) years of experience in result-based project/programme management, administration or related area is required. Experience in trade-related technical assistance, business support or related field is required.
  • Experience working with trade-related institutions and/or private sector networks in the South Asian countries of relevance to the programme is required. Experience supporting Asian LDCs, graduating LDCs and/or countries undergoing transitions in preferential market access arrangements is desirable. Experience working with UN, EU and/or other development agencies is desirable.
  • Experience of implementing European Union (EU) projects is desirable.

COMPETENCIES:

Professionalism:

In-depth knowledge of international trade and value chains in the South Asian countries of relevance to the programme, including institutional and private-sector challenges affecting participation in international trade. Knowledge of emerging trade issues relevant to the programme, including preferential market access, trade policy and facilitation, sustainable value chains, EU sustainability and due-diligence requirements, and inclusive trade. Solid understanding of trade-related technical assistance and results-based management of development programmes. Knowledge and understanding of theories, concepts and approaches relevant to particular sector, functional area or other specialized field. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow: empowers others to translate vision into results; is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; drives for change and improvements; does not accept the status quo; shows the courage to take unpopular stands. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing.

Languages: Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of language(s) spoken in participating South Asian countries is desirable.

Additional Information

This contract will be administered on behalf of ITC by UNOPS. Applicants must be authorized to work in the duty station where the position is located. Eligible applicants selected from outside the duty station are responsible for any expenses in connection with their relocation to the duty station.

Handicap International Federation (HI) is an independent and impartial aid organization, created in 1982, working across 63 countries. Join Our Mission to Foster Prosperity in Asia

Are you ready to make a difference in the future of Asia and be a catalyst for positive change? We are thrilled to offer a unique opportunity to become an important part of the prestigious Asian Development Bank (ADB). At ADB, our mission is simple yet powerful: to alleviate poverty and promote sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific region.

Organizational Setting and Reporting Relationship

The position of Senior Financial Management Officer is assigned to the Financial Management Division (PFFM) within the Procurement, Portfolio and Financial Management Department (PPFD). You will be based at our Nepal Resident Mission (NRM) Office in Kathmandu, Nepal.

You will report to Director, PFFM or a designated international staff and matrixed to Country Director, NRM. You will oversee junior team members.

Your Role

As a Senior Financial Management Officer, you will provide operational services in conducting financial management tasks for projects during all stages of the operational cycle, including processing, implementation, and completion. Additionally, you will support country, sector, and agency financial management assessments, and FM systems and capacity development strengthening programs. Furthermore, you will coordinate the delivery of knowledge sharing and capacity building support. Though the position is based in Nepal, you can be assigned to work on tasks in other developing member countries of ADB.

You will:

Operational services

  • Lead financial due diligence for project processing. This includes conducting FM assessments and financial and sustainability analyses, preparing cost estimates and financing plans, designing risk mitigation measures and covenants, and agreeing financial management, reporting and audit arrangements for the project.
  • Support project implementation through FM review missions, monitoring of FM action plans, coordination with project teams and executing agencies/ implementing agencies (EA/IAs), and maintenance of project data in ADB systems.
  • Lead annual project financial statement (APFS) and audited entity financial statement (AEFS) reviews for assigned projects; monitor compliance, quality issues, follow‑up actions, and financial covenant compliance.
  • Provide FM support to project teams and EA/IAs.

Country FM Systems

  • Participate as a team member in the country partnership strategy, governance assessments, and country public financial management assessments.
  • Support country, sector and agency FM systems assessments and help design and implement the regional FM strategic work plan.

Knowledge management

  • Participate and facilitate in FM training, conferences, and knowledge‑building activities, and organize/design FM capacity‑building programs and technical assistance for clients.
  • Develop and deliver FM training for EAs/IAs on ADB requirements.

Other tasks

  • Other tasks as assigned and reflected in your workplan.

Qualifications

You will need:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field; preferably with master’s degree or equivalent.
  • Professional qualification in accounting (e.g. CPA, CA, ACCA) from an internationally recognized institution by IFAC.
  • At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in private or public sector financial management (i.e., in accounting, budgeting, auditing); and at least 4 years of supervisory experience.
  • Experience with international financial institutions for sovereign and non-sovereign operations is advantageous.
  • Advanced knowledge in international and national accounting, reporting and auditing standards for the public sector.
  • Proficiency in expressing ideas in both spoken and written formats (and report-writing) in the local language and in English.
  • Demonstrated experience liaising and working with teams including government officials in Nepal.
  • Demonstrated capacity to guide staff to facilitate work planning, delivery and quality review.
  • Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and familiarity with database management tools.
  • Please refer to the link for ADB Competency Framework for TL6.

Benefits

ADB offers a rewarding salary and a comprehensive benefits package. The salary will be based on ADB’s standards and comparator markets, taking into account your qualifications and experience.

  • Retirement plan
  • Medical and health benefits
  • Paid leave (including parental)
  • Life and other insurance plans
  • Staff development

Additional Information

This appointment is open to internal and external applicants.

This opening is a local staff position. It is open only to nationals and permanent residents of Nepal.

This is a fixed term appointment with option to renew, initially for a period of up to 3 years, or up to the Normal Retirement Date (NRD), whichever comes earlier, for the purpose(s) and conditions determined by ADB, in accordance with Administrative Order No. 2.01 (Recruitment and Appointment). After the initial fixed-term period, ADB may choose to renew the appointment for up to an additional 3 years or not renewed. This decision will be made in the overall interest of ADB, based on factors including but not limited to the requirement of Staff’s particular blend of skills and experience for the medium-term work program of the organizational unit, sufficient funding to cover the renewed period, and Staff’s performance and suitability for employment. There is no limit to the number of renewals up to NRD. However, this appointment is not convertible to a regular appointment.

About Us

ADB is a leading multilateral development bank supporting inclusive, resilient, and sustainable growth across Asia and the Pacific. Working with its members and partners to solve complex challenges together, ADB harnesses innovative financial tools and strategic partnerships to transform lives, build quality infrastructure, and safeguard our planet. Founded in 1966, ADB is headquartered in Manila and owned by 69 members—50 from the region.

ADB only hires nationals of its 69 members.

title.rendered: Admin and Finance Assistant, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, Project Coordinator, Education Educator, Agriculture Technician

content.rendered:
Group of Helping Hands (SAHAS) Nepal is a non-profit making non-governmental-organization founded in 1996. Since then, SAHAS Nepal has been engaging in social mobilization, grassroots organisation/Community-Based Network Organisation (CBNO) formation and enhancing their capacity through partnership and implementing diverse programme and projects in the sectors of sustainable agriculture and food security, climate change, and education in 21 districts of Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal will be implementing an education project in Siraha district in Arnama and Bishnupur Rural Municipalities. The aim of the project is to enhance quality in education through an inclusive educational environment for children and improved livelihoods of parents in Siraha district. SAHAS Nepal is seeking energetic, committed and creative candidates to work on the education project aimed at enhancing the quality of education for the following positions, which will be based in Siraha district.

Position: Project Coordinator

Required no: 1

Academic Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, or a related field, with at least 5 years of relevant experience in the education sector, preferably Master’s degree with at least 3 years of relevant experience in the education sector
  • Proven project management experience, including planning, organizing, and managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating with Rural Municipalities, schools, teachers, and other education stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; ability to engage effectively with stakeholders at community, municipal, district, and provincial levels.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate, coach, and inspire project staff.
  • Knowledge of Nepal’s education system, policies, learning theories, and pedagogical strategies; familiarity with broader development work is an asset.
  • Prior experience working in rural communities, preferably in the Terai or similar geographic contexts.
  • Fluency in Maithili is highly preferred; strong command of Nepali and English (written and spoken).
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and basic data management tools.

Major Responsibilities

Project Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring

  • Lead overall project implementation in alignment with project goals, logframe, and detailed implementation plan.
  • Prepare annual, quarterly, and monthly work plans and ensure timely execution of activities as per project documents.
  • Collaborate with technical service providers to implement learning programs, training modules, and teaching–learning materials.
  • Manage project budgets, ensure expenditures comply with donor guidelines, and prepare budget reports as required by funding partners.
  • Track project progress, identify bottlenecks, document challenges and best practices, and recommend adaptive management actions.
  • Conduct regular field visits to assess program effectiveness, provide on-site coaching, and identify areas for improvement.

Coordination and Collaboration

  • Establish and maintain strong coordination with local government units (Rural Municipalities), education units, schools, teachers, and other relevant stakeholders at municipal, district, and provincial levels.
  • Liaise with project teams, partners, and key development facilitators to ensure smooth implementation and resource sharing.
  • Represent SAHAS Nepal at community, municipal, and district forums; ensure effective communication and cooperation with all stakeholders.
  • Facilitate community engagement activities to promote ownership and sustainability of project interventions.

Staff Mobilization, Monitoring, and Performance Review

  • Lead, mentor, and supervise project staff; provide regular coaching, capacity-building sessions, and performance feedback.
  • Mobilize staff according to project needs across Arnama and Bishnupur Rural Municipalities.
  • Conduct periodic performance reviews and support professional development of team members.

Report Writing and Documentation

  • Prepare timely progress reports (monthly, quarterly, annual) aligned with project goals and donor requirements.
  • Document key activities, lessons learned, case studies, and best practices for internal learning and external sharing.
  • Ensure proper filing and archiving of project documents, reports, and monitoring data.

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer

Required no: 1

Academic Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Development Studies, Social Science, Statistics, or a related field; Master’s preferred.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in M&E for education or development projects, preferably in rural or Terai contexts.
  • Strong experience with data collection and analysis tools (e.g., Kobo Toolbox, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, or similar).
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s education system, policies, and the broader development landscape.
  • Good computer skills (MS Office, especially Excel) and strong written and spoken English; Nepali required, Maithili preferred.
  • Experience designing surveys (baseline, midline, endline), indicators, and MEAL frameworks.
  • Strong analytical, reporting, and documentation skills; ability to translate data into actionable insights.

Major Responsibilities

Monitoring Planning and Indicator Development

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive Monitoring plan for the project.
  • Support the Project Coordinator in defining Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) at impact, outcome, output, and activity levels.
  • Ensure alignment of indicators with donor requirements and national education standards.

Data Management, Collection, and Analysis

  • Establish and maintain a project database to track progress against activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact.
  • Design and pilot data collection tools (surveys, checklists, feedback forms) for baseline, midline, and endline assessments.
  • Ensure accurate, timely, and ethical data collection, entry, cleaning, analysis, and visualization.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities in schools and communities and validate data quality.

Reporting, Documentation, and Learning

  • Generate periodic M&E reports (monthly, quarterly, annual) highlighting progress, trends, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Assist the Project Coordinator in preparing results-based reports of the project.
  • Document lessons learned, success stories, case studies, and best practices using text, photos, and video (with consent).
  • Organize capacity-building sessions for project staff on M&E tools, methodologies, and data use for decision-making.
  • Work closely with the project team to ensure all indicators are regularly monitored, reported, and used for adaptive management.

Position: Admin and Finance Assistant

Required Number: 1

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Studies (BBS), Business Administration (BBA), Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Minimum 1 year of relevant experience in finance, accounting, administration, procurement, or project support, preferably with an NGO/INGO or development organization.
  • Practical knowledge and experience in financial record keeping, bookkeeping, budget monitoring, procurement, and administrative management.
  • Good working knowledge of MS Excel, MS Word, PowerPoint, and accounting software.
  • Knowledge of government tax regulations, NGO financial procedures, donor compliance, and applicable organizational policies will be an advantage.
  • Good communication, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, integrity, and confidentiality in handling financial and administrative information.
  • Ability to work independently as well as effectively within a team and manage multiple tasks within deadlines.

Key Responsibilities

Finance and Accounting

  • Maintain day-to-day financial records and ensure accurate and timely recording of all financial transactions.
  • Maintain proper supporting documents, vouchers, bills, receipts, and other financial records in accordance compliance with organizational, government, and donor requirements.
  • Handle and maintain the project account and ensure proper documentation and reconciliation of project transactions.
  • Prepare periodic financial statements, expenditure reports, cash forecasts, and other financial information required by the project.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and identify variances for timely action.
  • Support the preparation, revision, and monitoring of the project budget in coordination with the Project Coordinator and relevant staff.
  • Ensure timely settlement of advances and maintain proper records of outstanding advances and liabilities.
  • Support internal and external audits and provide required financial documents and explanations.

Procurement and Logistics

  • Manage procurement-related processes in accordance with organizational procurement policies and donor requirements.
  • Obtain quotations, prepare procurement documentation, maintain supplier records, and ensure proper documentation of purchases.
  • Support the timely procurement and distribution of goods, materials, and services required for project implementation.
  • Maintain records of project assets, equipment, stock, and inventory.
  • Ensure the safe custody and appropriate use of project assets and materials.

Administration and Human Resources Support

  • Manage day-to-day administrative and logistical requirements of the project.
  • Maintain project-related personnel records, attendance, leave, contracts, and other administrative documents.
  • Ensure proper filing and safeguarding of administrative, financial, procurement, and personnel documents.

Coordination, Reporting and Compliance

  • Provide financial and administrative information required for project monitoring and reporting.
  • Perform other finance and administrative duties assigned by the supervisor in support of effective project implementation.

Position: Education Educator

Required Number: 2

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Minimum Intermediate level education; a Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Work, Development Studies, Sociology, or a related field will be preferred.
  • At least 1 year of relevant experience in community mobilization, education, child development, social development, or development projects.
  • Experience working with schools, teachers, parents, children/adolescents, community groups, and local government stakeholders will be an advantage.
